prompt:
Use case: illustration-story. PRODUCTION REFERENCE SHEET, landscape, not a finished book page. Bold clean clear 2D children's cartoon throughout, crisp continuous dark outlines, flat clean colors, restrained smooth cel shading, no painted or grainy texture, no gouache, no embossed relief, no 3D. Original friendly readable illustration. Ordinary neutral settings; no flags, religious/political symbols or costumes. No logos, text, letters, numbers, pseudo-writing, captions, watermarks or page borders. Natural anatomy and coherent hand/prop contact. Essential content at least 8 percent inside every edge.
 No named child cast: Kit and Zoe MUST NOT appear. Include unnamed human workers/adults ONLY when explicitly required by this particular scene; otherwise show only the natural subjects. Preserve exact reference identity and clothing.
Book: Marks on the Moon; World Discovery; nonfiction.
Setting: The Moon’s gray rocky surface and black sky, moving from distant sphere to explicit illustrative close views. No people or vehicles.
Design locks for the book's recurring subjects/props (NOT a visibility list; never insert later objects/states prematurely): Gray cratered Moon; One incoming gray space rock; Bowl-shaped crater with raised rim; Scattered fragments and overlapping smaller crater
 Create a clean separated reference board on white: show the principal recurring props/animals in front, side and three-quarter views, their relative scale beside any named human cast, and a single simple location key showing the persistent setting and daylight/palette. The human character model sheet is a supporting identity reference, not content to copy wholesale. Show only the subjects this book requires. Use initial object states: No face, cheese holes or stars visible through Moon; craters are surface depressions.. For orientation, the opening location/action is: Gray Moon shown large against black space with several clear circular craters and dark plains. Exact continuity: No face, cheese holes or stars visible through Moon; craters are surface depressions.. Do not show a completed craft or later scene merely because the finished object is listed in design locks. No future story events, no captions.

visualReview.note: Directly inspected Moon/rock/crater model board: crisp 2D gray forms, natural depressions, no atmosphere or text; reference is not a finished reading page.
